sections.heading: Did You Know?
paragraph: Scammers often pretend to be banks, delivery companies, government agencies, technology support, or family members.
Pressure and urgency are deliberate. A message that demands immediate payment, secrecy, or account access should be checked through a trusted contact method.
Antivirus cannot stop scams that convince someone to send money, share a password, or approve account access.

sections.heading: Who This Helps
paragraph: This service is for individuals, families, caregivers, and small businesses that want help recognizing phone, email, text, website, and payment scams.
It can help before a loss, after a close call, or whenever you are unsure whether a message or caller is legitimate.

sections.heading: Signs Scam Protection Would Help
items: You receive suspicious calls, texts, emails, or pop-ups that demand money, passwords, or immediate action
You want help recognizing fake banks, package alerts, technology support, or government messages
You clicked a suspicious link, shared information, or gave someone remote access
You help a family member who needs clearer guidance and safer device settings
You want practical scam education without jargon or scare tactics

sections.heading: What We Do
paragraph: We review the situation calmly, explain the warning signs, and help reduce the chance that the same tactic works again.
items: Explain common phone, email, text, website, and payment scams
Show how urgency, impersonation, secrecy, and unusual payment requests are used
Review safer settings for computers, phones, browsers, email, and calls
Help evaluate suspicious messages and identify the next steps
Secure risky settings after a scare or close call

sections.heading: When Another Service May Be a Better Fit
paragraph: Choose Scam and Fraud Protection for prevention, education, or help responding to suspicious messages.
If a computer may be infected, choose [Virus and Malware Removal](/services/virus-removal).
If passwords, account access, or multi-factor authentication need attention, choose [Password Manager Setup and Account Security](/services/password-management).

faq.question: Do I still need scam protection if I already have antivirus?
faq.answer: Yes. Many scams rely on pressure and impersonation instead of malicious software. Antivirus cannot stop you from sending money, sharing information, or approving access in response to a convincing message.

faq.question: Can you help after I clicked a scam link or gave information to someone?
faq.answer: Yes. We can help assess what happened, secure affected devices and settings, and identify the next steps for passwords and accounts. Virus removal or account security work may also be necessary.

faq.question: Is this only for seniors?
faq.answer: No. Anyone can be targeted. This service is useful for individuals, families, caregivers, and small businesses that want practical help recognizing and responding to scams.
